evidence_scope: Seven downloaded public packages, verified ZIP SHA-256 and CRC, bounded GOO members, passive native-file parsing. No game execution, image rendering, stock dependency closure, network request or reuse clearance. Counts are archived resources, not unique playable skins.

findings.summary: Selectable skin rows, model files and personality registrations have different counts; validate registry arithmetic and dependency closure.

Phase 2 integration uses identical body bytes under three resource names; POV and external weapons are separate models. The same body bytes appear in the Al MacDonald compilation, without establishing copying direction.
Kyle carrying Jan adds torso-child node 18 with a nineteen-joint death KEY and global player-PUP override. Model-header reuse restrictions are narrower than original-pack distribution permission.
Six material variants share geometry and hierarchy text; their eighteen-node actor mapping differs from the familiar eighteen-node player mapping.
The walking droid uses eleven nodes, six matching KEY files and a dedicated PUP whose weapon role maps to HEAD node 2; flying variants have a different thirteen-node structure.
A Jabba hierarchy renamed ky.3do retains eighteen nodes but different semantic roles, so filename and node count cannot certify retargeting.
A personality conversion coordinates inventory, separate weapon models and cloak body states; both body states preserve the same measured node topology.
models.dat declares 56 rows but contains 58, repeating indices 18 and 19. Readme reports client/scoring limitations; engine response to the registry discrepancy was not tested.

All 1931 sampled MATs are indexed eight-bit resources; small rectangular textures and one-level mips dominate, while four geometry sets are common but not universal. No rendered quality conclusion follows.
Sound mappings and saber catalogs can accompany skins; a model-specific breathing effect implemented in the global player COG expands the merge and test surface.
